items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: I thought that Wynton was the only trumpet player.

ctx.x: Well you know he’s a very special kid to me because my wife Gwen knows his mother very well. And she headed up a program called STAR, Students Targeting Adult Responsibility. And they were basically responsible for his education. They’ve gotten funds from different sources, now even I kicked in a few bucks, and sent him to Berklee, you know? And he’s still at Berklee, so he came up the hard way, and he came up the soulful way.

Didn’t he? Because it shows. Johnny Pate, whom you know of course, from Chicago, Johnny lives in Las Vegas and he has a radio show on the UNLV station. And he plays Johnny Griffin’s thing with Roy Hargrove, often. And I’m so thrilled that he’s getting some airplay and some attention, because for a while there, I thought that Wynton was the only trumpet player.
Well there’s several of them out there.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Wynton was a little kid at the time. I had him come up and play on the bandstand.

ctx.x: We played at a place called Le Club, in the Hyatt. Wynton was a little kid at the time. I had him come up and play on the bandstand. The first – one of the first times that he played with a professional group. He played real good. I used to write to him. I used to call him the demon. I gave him – sent him a flugelhorn. I don’t think he ever played it, though. He’s still got his own.
